Investigated and root-caused the case-003 docbench harness-reliability finding: NOT a Docling/Torch/child-process reliability problem as initially suspected. normalize-docling.mjs (and, latently, normalize.mjs) had a standalone-execution convenience block at module scope reading process.argv[2], the same slot run.mjs populates with the real case ID; importing the module from run.mjs therefore re-ran normalizeDocling() at import time, before any adapter had run, throwing ENOENT whenever docling.raw.json did not already exist for that case (masked for case-002 all session because its stale raw artifact was never deleted; case-003s was repeatedly deleted while testing from a clean slate, which is what exposed it). Confirmed via a single-line, zero-subprocess reproduction. Fixed by guarding both blocks with the same on-direct-execution-only pattern already used in browser-fetch.mjs/acquire.mjs. 5/5 clean-slate npm run docbench -- case-003 runs now succeed; case-001 (8/11,8/11,9/11), case-002 (3/11,4/11,3/11), and case-003 (9/11,10/11,3/11) all reproduce byte-identical historical scores. 2 new regression tests added (28/28 passing). No Ground Truth/selection/source/evaluator/adapter file touched; no ADR added (bug fix, not a new decision). See reports/document-understanding/20260926_1737_Docbench_Harness_Reliability_Investigation.md.

Ran the CJK Spacing Strategy Layer Experiment: moved closeCjkWrapSpaces (previously Docling-only) to common.mjs as the shared implementation and applied it to both flat-line engines in normalize.mjs, after explicitly comparing 4 candidate architectural layers (extraction, engine-specific normalization, document-family interpretation, semantic-matching tolerance) and choosing engine-specific normalization on evidence -- PyMuPDF never exhibits the artifact, Docling already had its own independent instance of the identical rule, and the document-family-interpretation layer was explicitly ruled out per ADR-010 since the artifact is engine-specific (pdfjs-dist gap-threshold reconstruction), not engine-independent. Pre-registered expected impact before re-running; every prediction matched exactly: case-002 pdfjs-baseline 3/11->4/11, case-003 pdfjs-baseline 9/11->10/11 (both via item_name_present_among_candidates FAIL->PASS), case-001 and all Docling/PyMuPDF results byte-identical across all three cases. 8 new tests added (34/34 passing). No Ground Truth/selection/source/evaluator file touched; no ADR added (uses an already-established architectural pattern, ADR-010, not a new decision). See reports/document-understanding/20260926_1816_CJK_Spacing_Strategy_Layer_Experiment.md.

Ran a CJK Fullwidth-Punctuation Boundary safety experiment on the closeCjkWrapSpaces strategy established at bac939b. Exhaustively searched all six flat-line raw artifacts (pdfjs-baseline/pymupdf-baseline x case-001/002/003) for every fullwidth-punctuation-adjacent whitespace instance: every real occurrence either never reaches closeCjkWrapSpaces in practice (page-label lines that never match the row-extraction regexes) or is already inside the pre-existing, out-of-scope annotation-contamination value, with zero PASS/FAIL impact either way. A genuinely new boundary was found and confirmed beneficial: fullwidth digits (e.g. ６, U+FF16) fall inside the closable Unicode range (Halfwidth/Fullwidth Forms, FF00-FFEF) and correctly get their surrounding spaces closed in every real header-row instance across all three cases; no counter-example (a legitimate space destroyed inside an otherwise-correct value) was found. Decision: KEEP -- no production code changed. 8 new characterization tests added (43/43 passing), including one explicitly-marked-ambiguous case (ideographic-comma-adjacent spacing) documented as current behavior, not certified as correct. No benchmark rerun performed (production code unchanged, explained in the report). No Ground Truth/selection/source/evaluator file touched; no ADR added (confirms an existing decision, ADR-010, remains sound). Recommended next step: package case-003 for PR review rather than starting another normalization experiment. See reports/document-understanding/20260926_1935_CJK_Fullwidth_Punctuation_Boundary_Experiment.md.
